📅 Calendar & Festivals

A whole calendar in one roll: the reckoning and this year's name, the months and the days of the week, the seasons, the moons and their phases, and a festival for every month with what the party can do there.

The calendar tables are the Gazette's own. Festival checks name Pathfinder skills and saves, with DCs for a low-level party; moon phases are the same as the Travel tool's.
The address bar holds the calendar, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it. A new naming style renames the months and days but keeps the festivals; a new week length or climate keeps the months; another moon keeps the ones you have.
Holy days from the Pantheon tab can go on the calendar too.

⛪ Pantheon

A heaven's worth of gods in one roll: what each one rules, their domain, whether they're holy or unholy, holy symbol, holy day, what the faithful must and mustn't do, the temple and its priests, what they want from adventurers, and who they can't stand.

The pantheon tables are the Gazette's own. Domains use Pathfinder's cleric domain names, and the gods are the Gazette's own, so they fit any homebrew setting.
The address bar holds the pantheon, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it. More gods keeps the ones you have; a new shape keeps the gods but changes who rules and who feuds; a new naming style only renames them.
🐉 The World picker's Forgotten Realms names are used under the Fan Content Policy; every description is the Gazette's own, and no rules come with them.

🏛️ Factions

The powers of a town, a city, or a kingdom in one roll: guilds, cults, noble houses, thieves' rings, knightly orders, temples, mages, and sellswords. Each with a goal, a leader and lieutenants, a symbol, resources, a secret, rivals and allies, and a job for the party.

The faction tables are the Gazette's own. Leaders and lieutenants come from the Town Square's NPC generator, and each 🎭 button opens that person there in full.
The address bar holds the factions, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it. More factions keeps the ones you have; a new first faction changes that one (and any faction of that kind it trades places with); a new place changes only the numbers.
Temples and orders can follow the gods of the Pantheon tab.
🐉 The World picker's Forgotten Realms names are used under the Fan Content Policy; every description is the Gazette's own, and no rules come with them.

📜 History & Timeline

The ages of the world in one roll, each following from the last: foundings, empires, golden ages, wars, plagues, falls, and dark ages. Each with who mattered, the faith of the day, and the ruins, grudges, relics, and customs it left behind for the party to find today.

The history tables are the Gazette's own; the people who mattered are named by the Town Square's name tables.
The address bar holds the history, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it. More ages keeps the ones you have; a new span changes only the years; a new beginning rewrites everything after it.
The ages can name the gods of the Pantheon tab and date the factions of the Factions tab.

🏘️ Town Generator

A whole settlement in one roll, from a hamlet to a metropolis: who runs it, the watch, the temple and its god, the factions, its districts and buildings, the people worth knowing, its taverns and shops, the laws, the trouble, the rumors, and a job for the party.

The town tables are the Gazette's own. Its people come from the Town Square's NPC generator, its taverns and its quest from the DM Toolbox, its shops from the Shop page, and its rumors from the Tavern's rumor mill; every link opens the same one there.
The address bar holds the town, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it. A new size keeps the name, the temple, and the first people; a new place keeps the size and the people; new times change only the taverns, the shops, and what fines and bribes cost.
The temple and the factions can follow the gods of the Pantheon tab.
🐉 The World picker's Forgotten Realms names are used under the Fan Content Policy; every description is the Gazette's own, and no rules come with them.

🌳 Family Trees

A noble house, or the family of anyone your party deals with: the head of the house and their parents and grandparents, brothers, sisters, and cousins, children and grandchildren, the partners who married in, the dead, second marriages, and a secret or two. Change anyone, add or remove people, and keep it in your notebook.

The family tables are the Gazette's own. Everyone old enough opens on the Town Square's NPC page as the same person, family name and age included, and 📓 Save as an NPC files them in your notebook, linked to the family.
Every faction on the Factions tab, and every town ruled by a noble on the Town tab, has a 🌳 button that rolls the family around that same leader.
The address bar holds the rolled family, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it. Your changes live in your campaign notebook: open the same link again and they come back.

🏚️ Dungeons & Sites

A keyed adventure site in one roll: a crypt, a lost mine, a wizard's tower, a sunken temple, a bandit fort, a monster lair, a ruined keep, a sewer, a smugglers' cave, a shipwreck, a lighthouse, a haunted manor, or a barrow mound. You get its story, a map, and a key to every room, with a feature in each, the foes who hold the place, traps, someone else to meet in a room or two, wandering monsters, and a hoard at the end.

🗺️ Battle map for a VTT (PNG)

The map as a picture on a 5-foot grid, one square to a corridor's width, ready for Owlbear Rodeo, Foundry, Roll20, or any virtual tabletop. The rooms are squared up to the grid. The file name ends in the map's size in squares (for example 52x38), the number your VTT asks for.

The site tables are the Gazette's own. Its foes are Pathfinder creatures from Monster Core, Monster Core 2, and NPC Core, picked to the Encounter Builder's XP budgets from GM Core (all under the ORC license; see the notice), and every fight opens there; the hoard opens in the Loot generator. Trap, hazard, and door DCs follow GM Core's DC by level at the party's level; trap damage is the Gazette's own.
The address bar holds the site, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it. A new party level or size keeps the map, the rooms, and where the fights and traps are, and changes only the monsters, DCs, and damage; a new site size keeps the name, the story, and the first rooms.
A site can be dated to an age of the History tab.

🌍 Continent Generator

A map of a whole continent in one roll: coasts and islands, mountains, rivers running to the sea, forests, deserts, and swamps, climate bands from north to south, and the nations on it, each with its ruler, its towns, its exports, and a feud with a neighbor. Then the roads between the towns and the ruins, lairs, and towers worth the trip.

🗺️ Download the map (PNG)

The map as a picture, to share with your players or drop into a virtual tabletop. A journey you picked shows on it too, and so do your pins unless you untick them (to keep them from the players).

The map and its tables are the Gazette's own. Rulers come from the Town Square's NPC generator; every town opens on the Town tab inside its realm, every place worth the trip on the Sites tab, and every road or journey in the DM Toolbox's Travel tab with its terrain and miles filled in.
The address bar holds the map, so 🔗 Copy Link shares it (but not your pins: they stay in your notebook, in this browser). A new number of nations keeps the land; a new mix of land and sea raises or lowers the sea over the same ground; a new size is a new map.

🗺️ Your Maps

Bring your own map: a world from Inkarnate or Wonderdraft, a battle map from Dungeondraft, a photo of the one you drew on graph paper. Pan and zoom around it, drop numbered pins, name them, write a note on each, and link them to your notebook (a town, a site, a faction, a quest) so a click on the pin opens it. Keep as many maps as your campaign needs.

⬇️ Download the map

With your pins drawn on, at the picture's full size, to share with your players or drop into a virtual tabletop. Untick the pins to save the picture just as you uploaded it.

Your maps stay in this browser: the pictures in its storage for big files (IndexedDB), the names, notes, and pins in your campaign notebook. Nothing is uploaded anywhere. A picture can be a PNG, JPEG, or WebP of up to 25 MB and 16,384 pixels a side.
The notebook's 💾 Export carries each map's name, notes, and pins but not its picture; 💾 Back up everything carries the pictures too. Removing a map from the notebook deletes its picture.
Pins sit at a spot on the picture, so a new version of the same map (🔁 Replace Picture) keeps them where they were, even at another size.

📓 Campaign Notebook

Everything you save from the other tabs, the Town Square's NPCs, and the Toolbox's quests, in one place: a link back to each roll, your notes on it, and the threads between them (the town that keeps this pantheon's gods, the history those factions came out of). Log each game as a session and track the party's quests, then open the next game with 📣 Last Time On…. Export the whole world as a file to keep it safe or carry it to another browser.

🖨️ Print for Players

Tick what to hand out. Each roll comes back from its link with the secrets left out: 🔒 lines stay with you, 👁️ lines go to the players. Click a line to switch it, or ✏️ to put it in your own words; the notebook remembers. Rewording changes only the notebook's copy, never the roll. Rooms, foes, traps, and treasure never print, and neither do 🔒 DM-only notes.

The notebook lives in this browser only: nothing is sent anywhere, and clearing your browser's site data clears it too, so 💾 Export now and then, or back up everything the tools keep.
Each entry keeps the link that rolls it again, so a saved town comes back exactly as it was. Saving links a roll to the saved rolls it uses (a town or a history on a saved pantheon's gods, a history that dates saved factions); link anything else by hand under 📝 Notes and links.
A session holds its number, the date you played, what happened, the NPCs met, the loot handed out, and the threads left open. A quest holds its giver, its reward, and a status (🟡 open, ✅ done, ❌ failed) you change on the card. 📣 Last Time On… reads back the latest session that has a recap, with its open threads and every open quest, and prints it large enough to read aloud.
Every entry has 👁️ notes the players may see and 🔒 notes for you alone. 🖨️ Print for Players turns the entries you tick into parchment handouts: faction secrets, NPC secrets and hooks, how a site was lost and who holds it now, what a ruin means today, and who really rules a town all start out 🔒, and you can switch any line either way. Export and backups keep both kinds of notes.
📄 Word saves the player sheets (one entry to a page), the recap, or the whole notebook (every roll written out, 🔒 lines marked) as a Word file, which Google Docs opens too. 📋 Copy keeps the headings and bold when you paste into Google Docs or Word.
📂 Import adds a notebook file to this one; entries you already have keep your notes and gain the file's.

🕸️ The Web

Your notebook as a web: every saved entry, and a line wherever two of them meet. See which towns keep which gods, who sits in which family, where your map pins lead, and which threads hang loose. Hover or click an entry to light up everything tied to it.

🕸️ The notebook is empty, so there's no web yet.

Save rolls to the notebook from any tab, link them together, and they show up here.

The web is drawn from your campaign notebook, in this browser: nothing is sent anywhere. Three things draw a line: a link between two entries (saving links a roll to the saved rolls it uses; link anything else under 📝 Notes and links), a pin on a continent or one of your maps that opens another entry, and a family member linked to a saved NPC.
The first layout comes from your entries, so the same notebook lays out the same way anywhere. After that the web keeps its shape: a new entry finds a spot beside what it's tied to, and an entry you drag stays where you put it (📌 Let It Move frees it). 🧲 Tidy Up lets everything else settle; 🔀 Start Over lays the whole web out again.
⬇️ Download Picture saves the entries and lines showing (after your filters) as a PNG, with every name written out.

How the Campaign Map with Pins works

Upload a world from Inkarnate or Wonderdraft, a battle map from Dungeondraft, or a photo of the one you drew on graph paper: a PNG, JPEG, or WebP of up to 25 MB. Pan and zoom around it, drop numbered pins, name them, write a note on each, and link them to your notebook (a town, a site, a faction, a quest) so a click on the pin opens it. Keep as many maps as your campaign needs. Nothing is uploaded anywhere: the pictures stay in this browser, and the pins in your campaign notebook. 🔁 Replace Picture swaps in a new version and keeps the pins where they were.

At the table

  • Pin every town the party has visited, with a note on who they upset there.
  • Link a pin to a saved town or dungeon, and a click opens it mid-session.
  • 🖨️ Print the map with its numbered pins and key for the players' handout.
  • Redrew the map? Replace the picture and the pins stay put.

Works with

Pins link to anything in your Campaign Notebook and show up as lines in the Relationship Web. No map yet? Roll one with the Continent Map Generator.
